- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) or shows sharp declines, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1-2 days), leading to over-forecasting in subsequent days; apply lagged correction or dampen momentum.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike (e.g., price rises then falls), model often fails to recognize this; reduce forecast after peak, especially if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early days (1-5) when sentiment is volatile; cap forecast at 1-2% above recent 7-day average to avoid bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.3 → +0.3), model often misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth out false signals.
- When sentiment is flat or near-zero, model often drifts toward historical mean; apply mean-reversion correction if forecast deviates >1.5σ from recent 14-day average.
